Usage: gridstator [options] [command]

Gridstator: multiple machines, one workflow. Run builds and tests on your LAN
cluster.

Options:
  -v, --version               output the version number
  -h, --help                  display help for command

Commands:
  login [options] <url>       Connect this machine to a controller (verifies the
                              CA fingerprint and token)
  status [options]            Show cluster, node and job summary
  nodes [options]             List and manage worker nodes
  jobs [options]              List jobs (most recent first)
  job [options] <id>          Show details of one job
  run [options] [command...]  Run a command in a container on a cluster node,
                              against a snapshot of this project
  logs [options] <id>         Print a job's logs
  cancel <id>                 Cancel a queued or running job
  retry [options] <id>        Run a finished job again with the same snapshot
                              and settings
  snapshot [options]          Capture this project as a snapshot and upload it
                              (shows what would be sent)
  token                       Manage client and join tokens (admin)
  groups [options]            List job groups (sharded runs), most recent first
  group                       Inspect and control a job group (sharded run)
  init [options]              Create a gridstator.yml in the current project
  agents                      Keep worker agents on the controller’s build
                              (status, updates, auto-update)
  build [options] [context]   Build a Docker image from this project on a
                              cluster node (BuildKit)
  actions                     Run GitHub Actions workflows on the cluster with
                              act
  artifacts [options] <id>    List or download the artifacts of a job
  doctor [options]            Check this machine's setup and the connection to
                              the controller
  controller                  Run and manage the cluster controller
  agent                       Run a worker agent on this machine
  help [command]              display help for command

  status [options]            Show cluster, node and job summary
  nodes [options]             List and manage worker nodes
  jobs [options]              List jobs (most recent first)
  job [options] <id>          Show details of one job
  run [options] [command...]  Run a command in a container on a cluster node,
                              against a snapshot of this project
  logs [options] <id>         Print a job's logs
  cancel <id>                 Cancel a queued or running job
  retry [options] <id>        Run a finished job again with the same snapshot
                              and settings
  snapshot [options]          Capture this project as a snapshot and upload it
                              (shows what would be sent)
  token                       Manage client and join tokens (admin)
  groups [options]            List job groups (sharded runs), most recent first
  group                       Inspect and control a job group (sharded run)
  init [options]              Create a gridstator.yml in the current project
  agents                      Keep worker agents on the controller’s build
                              (status, updates, auto-update)
  build [options] [context]   Build a Docker image from this project on a
                              cluster node (BuildKit)
  actions                     Run GitHub Actions workflows on the cluster with
                              act
  artifacts [options] <id>    List or download the artifacts of a job
  doctor [options]            Check this machine's setup and the connection to
                              the controller
  controller                  Run and manage the cluster controller
  agent                       Run a worker agent on this machine
  help [command]              display help for command

Usage: gridstator run [options] [command...]

Run a command in a container on a cluster node, against a snapshot of this
project

Arguments:
  command                  command to run (after --). A single argument is run
                           with sh -c

Options:
  -t, --task <name>        run a task defined in gridstator.yml
  --image <image>          container image (default from gridstator.yml, else
                           node:24-bookworm)
  --node <node>            run on this node (name or id)
  -l, --label <label>      require a node label (repeatable) (default: [])
  --cpus <n>               CPUs to reserve and limit the container to
  --memory <size>          memory to reserve and limit the container to, e.g. 4g
  -e, --env <NAME=value>   environment variable (repeatable) (default: [])
  -s, --secret-env <NAME>  forward a secret from this shell; masked in logs
                           (repeatable) (default: [])
  --timeout <duration>     stop the job after this long, e.g. 30m
  --priority <n>           higher runs first (-100..100)
  --retries <n>            automatic retries if the node is lost
  --name <name>            display name for the job
  --shell                  run the arguments as one shell command (sh -c)
  -a, --artifact <path>    collect a file or directory as an artifact after the
                           run (repeatable) (default: [])
  --shards <n>             split into N parallel shards across workers; use
                           {shard} and {total} in the command
  --prefer <node>          prefer this worker when it can take the job
                           (repeatable) (default: [])
  --no-snapshot            do not send the project; run in an empty /workspace
  -d, --detach             print the job id and exit instead of streaming logs
  --json                   print the submitted job as JSON (implies --detach)
  -h, --help               display help for command

cases.stderr:
Usage: gridstator controller [options] [command]

Run and manage the cluster controller

Options:
  -h, --help                         display help for command

Commands:
  local                              Manage the controller owned by this account
                                     (used by the VS Code extension)
  init [options]                     Create a new cluster: CA, server
                                     certificate, database and an admin token
  start [options]                    Run the controller in the foreground
  publish-build [options] [tarball]  Switch the controller to another build,
                                     which workers then follow: this CLI's own
                                     bundled build, or a gridstator .tgz (admin)
  token                              Recovery: issue client tokens directly in
                                     the controller database
  install-service [options]          Run the controller as a systemd service
                                     that starts at boot
  uninstall-service [options]        Stop and remove the controller systemd
                                     service (keeps data)
  help [command]                     display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller local [options] [command]

Manage the controller owned by this account (used by the VS Code extension)

Options:
  -h, --help                  display help for command

Commands:
  status [options]            Inspect local ownership, endpoint and user-service
                              state
  ensure-login [options]      Reuse or create one shared local admin login
                              without printing credentials
  service [options] <action>  Control the local controller user service
  configure [options]         Apply a coordinated endpoint change and restart,
                              recovering on failure
  help [command]              display help for command

cases.stdout:
Usage: gridstator nodes [options] [command]

List and manage worker nodes

Options:
  --json                   machine-readable output
  -h, --help               display help for command

Commands:
  show [options] <node>
  set [options] <node>     Change scheduling settings for a node
  enable <node>            Allow the scheduler to place jobs on a node
  disable <node>           Stop placing new jobs on a node (running jobs
                           continue)
  drain <node>             Stop placing new jobs on a node and let running jobs
                           finish
  remove [options] <node>  Remove a node and revoke its credential (admin)

Usage: gridstator run [options] [command...]

Run a command in a container on a cluster node, against a snapshot of this
project

Arguments:
  command                  command to run (after --). A single argument is run
                           with sh -c

Options:
  -t, --task <name>        run a task defined in gridstator.yml
  --image <image>          container image (default from gridstator.yml, else
                           node:24-bookworm)
  --node <node>            run on this node (name or id)
  -l, --label <label>      require a node label (repeatable) (default: [])
  --cpus <n>               CPUs to reserve and limit the container to
  --memory <size>          memory to reserve and limit the container to, e.g. 4g
  -e, --env <NAME=value>   environment variable (repeatable) (default: [])
  -s, --secret-env <NAME>  forward a secret from this shell; masked in logs
                           (repeatable) (default: [])
  --timeout <duration>     stop the job after this long, e.g. 30m
  --priority <n>           higher runs first (-100..100)
  --retries <n>            automatic retries if the node is lost
  --name <name>            display name for the job
  --shell                  run the arguments as one shell command (sh -c)
  -a, --artifact <path>    collect a file or directory as an artifact after the
                           run (repeatable) (default: [])
  --shards <n>             split into N parallel shards across workers; use
                           {shard} and {total} in the command
  --prefer <node>          prefer this worker when it can take the job
                           (repeatable) (default: [])
  --no-snapshot            do not send the project; run in an empty /workspace
  -d, --detach             print the job id and exit instead of streaming logs
  --json                   print the submitted job as JSON (implies --detach)
  -h, --help               display help for command

cases.stdout:
Usage: gridstator controller [options] [command]

Run and manage the cluster controller

Options:
  -h, --help                         display help for command

Commands:
  local                              Manage the controller owned by this account
                                     (used by the VS Code extension)
  init [options]                     Create a new cluster: CA, server
                                     certificate, database and an admin token
  start [options]                    Run the controller in the foreground
  publish-build [options] [tarball]  Switch the controller to another build,
                                     which workers then follow: this CLI's own
                                     bundled build, or a gridstator .tgz (admin)
  token                              Recovery: issue client tokens directly in
                                     the controller database
  install-service [options]          Run the controller as a systemd service
                                     that starts at boot
  uninstall-service [options]        Stop and remove the controller systemd
                                     service (keeps data)
  help [command]                     display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller init [options]

Create a new cluster: CA, server certificate, database and an admin token

Options:
  --data-dir <dir>  controller data directory (default: "/V1_DATA/controller")
  --host <host>     address to listen on (default: "0.0.0.0")
  --port <port>     port to listen on (default: "7300")
  --san <names...>  extra hostnames/IPs for the server certificate
  --force           create a new cluster even if one exists (the old data
                    directory is backed up)
  --no-login        do not save the admin credentials as this machine's client
                    configuration
  -h, --help        display help for command
